exercises.title: A Different Kind of Morning
exercises.text:
Anna is a nurse. She works at a hospital in the centre of the city. Most people start work at nine, but Anna's day is different. She gets up at half past five, has a quick breakfast and takes the first bus at six.

Her shift starts at seven and finishes at three in the afternoon. After work, she usually goes to the gym or meets a friend for coffee. In the evening she reads or watches a film. She goes to bed early, at about ten o'clock.

Anna likes her job because she helps people every day. The only thing she doesn't like is the early start, especially in winter when it is still dark outside.

How does Anna travel to work?

exercises.title: Is Remote Work Here to Stay?
exercises.text:
Ten years ago, working from home was a privilege enjoyed by only a few employees. Today, millions of people work remotely at least part of the week. Supporters say it saves time and money: there is no daily commute, and people can organise their day more flexibly.

However, remote work also has disadvantages. Some employees feel isolated and miss the informal conversations that happen in an office. Managers sometimes find it harder to build a team spirit, and new staff may take longer to learn how the company works.

As a result, many companies have chosen a hybrid model, where employees spend two or three days in the office and the rest at home. Although nobody knows exactly how work will look in the future, it seems unlikely that we will completely return to the old ways.

questions.prompt: According to supporters, what is one benefit of remote work?
Which problem is mentioned for new staff?
options: They learn company processes more slowly

questions.prompt: A hybrid model means working only from home.

options: Everyone will return to the office
